questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2 \cos x dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Tabular: $x^2 \to 2x \to 2 \to 0$; $\cos x \to \sin x \to -\cos x \to -\sin x$. Alternating: $+x^2\sin x - 2x(-\cos x) + 2(-\sin x) = x^2\sin x + 2x\cos x - 2\sin x + C$.

questions.q: Evaluate the cyclic integral $I = \int e^x \sin x dx$.
questions.answer: Integrate by parts twice: $I = e^x \sin x - \int e^x \cos x dx = e^x \sin x - [e^x \cos x - \int e^x (-\sin x)dx] = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) - I \Rightarrow 2I = e^x(\sin x - \cos x) \Rightarrow I = \frac{1}{2}e^x(\sin x - \cos x) + C$.
$\int \ln x dx = x\ln x - x$. Evaluating from 1 to $e$: $[e\ln e - e] - [1\ln 1 - 1] = [e - e] - [0 - 1] = 0 - (-1) = 1$.

questions.q: Which trigonometric substitution is best suited to evaluate $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{16 - x^2}} dx$?
questions.answer: For forms $\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$, the substitution $x = a\sin\theta$ simplifies the radical via $16 - 16\sin^2\theta = 16\cos^2\theta$.
Standard formula $\int \frac{1}{x^2 + a^2} dx = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{a}\right) + C$. With $a = 4$: $\frac{1}{4}\arctan\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) + C$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Integrals of Powers of Trigonometric Functions

questions.answer: Rewrite $\sin^3 x = (1 - \cos^2 x)\sin x$. Let $u = \cos x, du = -\sin x dx$: $\int -(1 - u^2) du = -u + \frac{u^3}{3} + C = -\cos x + \frac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + C$.
Use double angle identity $\cos^2 x = \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2}$: $\int \frac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2} dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{\sin(2x)}{4} + C$.
Identity: $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$. Integrating: $\int (\sec^2 x - 1) dx = \tan x - x + C$.
Let $u = 1 + e^x, du = e^x dx$. At $x = 0, u = 2$; at $x = 1, u = 1 + e$. $\int_2^{1+e} \frac{1}{u} du = [\ln|u|]_2^{1+e} = \ln(1 + e) - \ln 2 = \ln\left(\frac{1 + e}{2}\right)$.
Let $u = \ln x, du = \frac{1}{x}dx$. $\int \frac{1}{u} du = \ln|u| + C = \ln|\ln x| + C$.
